verdict.rationale: Pinecone documents hybrid search combining keyword (BM25) and semantic signals over a single index. Fusion ranking, however, is described as fusing separate searches with reciprocal rank fusion, and `score_by` ranks by one signal per search. That makes it two approaches (a text-match filter on a dense search, or RRF across multiple searches) rather than a clearly single fused query. A community user corroborates the combined keyword+vector search. missing for 10: documented single-request server-side fusion of dense and sparse/BM25 scores, clarity on whether RRF runs server-side or client-side, hands-on corroboration of fusion ranking quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can combine dense vector search with keyword or sparse (BM25-style) signals in one hybrid query with fusion ranking

citations.quote: Combine keyword and semantic retrieval in Pinecone with a text-match filter on a dense search, or by fusing separate searches with reciprocal rank fusion.
Hybrid search combines a keyword signal with a semantic signal so a single query benefits from both.
A single index can serve full-text search (BM25 with Lucene queries), semantic search, and sparse-vector search together
When you search, you rank results via `score_by`: `text` (BM25), `query_string` (Lucene), `dense_vector`, or `sparse_vector`.
there is more than meets the eye with the combined keyword+vector search and handling of filtering
